Smart Baby Cradle

Dec 2023 to Mar 2024 Team project, 4 members

A wirelessly monitored infant cradle. A motion sensor detects the baby stirring, the cradle rocks automatically, and caregivers get a real-time alert. The interesting part was getting two controllers to cooperate reliably.

ControllersArduino Uno, ESP32
SensorMPU6050
BusesI2C, UART
LanguageC, Embedded C

What I did

  • Brought up the two-controller system and defined the Arduino Uno to ESP32 integration interface
  • Coordinated the four-person team and set module ownership
  • Led iterative test cycles to debug sensor timing, documenting reliability improvements each round

Delivered a working prototype and the final project presentation.

ControllerNodeMCU

Wi-Fi Surveillance Car

Aug 2023 to Nov 2023 Team project, 4 members

Most remote-control cars run on radio links with limited range and no live view. We built a ground-based surveillance car that is driven over Wi-Fi from a phone app and streams live video to any phone or computer on the same network.

ControllersNodeMCU (ESP8266), ESP32-CAM
DriveL298N, 4 x 12 V DC motors
ControlBlynk app over Wi-Fi
VideoESP32-CAM stream in any browser

What I did

  • Proposed the concept of a Wi-Fi ground vehicle as an alternative to range-limited radio control
  • Integrated the NodeMCU, L298N motor driver, and motors, and set up the ESP32-CAM video stream on a shared hotspot
  • Designed the Blynk control layout: forward, backward, left, right, and a speed slider

Presented a working prototype that streamed live video while being driven from a phone.

GPS Sensor Driver and Error Analysis

Sep 2026 to present Coursework, Robotics Sensing and Navigation

A ROS 2 driver that turns raw NMEA sentences from a USB GPS receiver into UTM positions, followed by a study of how much the position wanders when the sky is open versus blocked.

LanguagePython
FrameworkROS 2, custom message
InputNMEA $GPGGA over serial

What I did

  • Wrote the driver node: read serial NMEA, parse $GPGGA fixes, convert latitude and longitude to UTM, publish at 1 Hz
  • Collected stationary and walking datasets with rosbag
  • Analyzed positional error and scatter under open-sky versus signal-occluded conditions

Documented the findings in a technical report.

Lidar Noise Characterization and Scan Matching

Fall 2026 Coursework, Robotics Sensing and Navigation

How noisy is a 2-D lidar, and does it match its datasheet? I characterized the sensor from repeated static scans, then used that understanding to estimate robot motion between two scans.

ToolsNumPy, Matplotlib
Data100 static scans
MethodsLeast squares, gradient descent, L1 robust loss

What I did

  • Fit a closed-form, range-dependent noise model that matched the manufacturer's datasheet specification
  • Implemented least squares and gradient descent from scratch and validated them on held-out scan points
  • Handled corrupted feature matches with automatic outlier rejection and an L1 robust loss

Alignment error dropped from 0.52 m to 0.04 m.
